Chapter Eight: Troubleshooting Stubborn Challenges—When Change Feels Impossible
Let’s be honest—some habits just don’t want to budge. We all have those sticky behaviors that seem glued in place, don’t we?
Maybe it’s something tied to a deep emotion, part of your identity, or a routine you’ve had for years. When you hit a wall and progress grinds to a halt, it’s so easy to feel defeated, like change is just out of reach. But here’s the thing—even the most stubborn challenges can be unraveled if you go back to the six sources of influence and look for the levers you might’ve missed.
Think of it like this: imagine you’re standing in front of a locked door, and there are six different keys on your keyring. If one key doesn’t work, what do you do? You try another, or maybe even a combination of a few. The solution isn’t always about pushing harder—it’s about trying a new approach.
Here are a few advanced troubleshooting techniques you can use:
First, try doubling up on your sources. Let’s say social pressure is really strong—like you feel pushed to drink at every party. The answer? Strengthen several other sources at once, maybe by boosting your personal motivation, setting up your environment for success, and building a support team.
Second, sometimes you need a bigger shake-up. A tiny tweak might not cut it. If you’re stuck in a rut, a radical change—like switching jobs, moving to a new area, or joining a whole new group—can help break those old patterns wide open.
Third, try reframing your goal. If the change you want feels totally out of reach, don’t be afraid to shift the target a little. Focus on getting better, not being perfect. Even small wins can have a huge impact.
Picture someone who’s tried to quit smoking again and again, without luck. Now, imagine they join a support group for social motivation, use nicotine patches or gum for structural help, and set up a reward for every smoke-free day—a boost of structural motivation. By layering those different sources together, their odds of success go way up.
And don’t forget, sometimes the best way forward is to get a fresh perspective. A coach, a therapist, or even a trusted friend can help you spot things you might miss on your own.
So, here’s the real takeaway: when change feels impossible, it’s usually a sign that one or more sources of influence need some attention—or maybe just a totally new angle.
Persistence, creativity, and support—they’re your best friends on this journey.
